changelog: Replace O1 to prefer assertion-ending cuts (and, if tied, the later one) to correct the prompt's bias for earlier intra-clause cuts that produced harmful misorderings.
findings: The prompt prefers earlier intra-clause cuts over markers that end a self-contained assertion, misordering cuts that leave the preceding stretch as a full statement (later assertion-ending cuts are safer).

The prompt treats as acceptable cuts that detach a short sentence-final complement (object/complement or quoted title/measurement/location), producing misleading or contradictory preceding fragments when that small tail is withheld.

edits.now: Prefer the marker that ends a self-contained assertion over an earlier marker in

diagnosis.why: Changing O1 to prefer markers that end a self-contained assertion pushed the scorer to pick later, assertion-ending cuts and avoid earlier intra-clause cuts; that shift improved cohesion for longer-latency bins (≤10 and overall) but degraded short-latency bins (≤3 and ≤5). Rank_depth drops at the top positions show the edit changed the model's early choices (so it could and did hurt short-budget behavior), and the tails illustrate this trade — e.g. better grouping of names/enumerations but worse attachment/splitting of dependent clauses like the 'Symptoms, such as vomiting...' example.
diagnosis.lesson: Do not globally prefer later assertion-ending markers at the cost of removing earlier intra-clause cut candidates needed by short-latency budgets; preserve early cut options (or scope the preference) so short-depth rankings are not degraded.
